chunks: and feel ashamed of running away, because it is a shame for posterity and (cause of awarding you) fire on the Day of Judgement.
and walk towards death with ease.
because Satan is hiding in its corner.
He has extended his hand for assault
and has kept back his foot for running away.
till the light of Truth dawns upon you.
“While ye have the upper hand, and Allāh is with you, and never will He depreciate your deeds.”

key_terms.السَّوَاد: the black mass / great majority (of troops)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of patience and avoiding shame in battle according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage, delivered during the Battle of Siffin, specifically exhorts Imam Ali to adhere to the 'Sawad al-A'zam' (the main body of his army), a strategic and symbolic directive to maintain unity and avoid fragmentation. It contrasts the shame of retreat with the dignity of steadfastness, framing the conflict as a spiritual struggle where Satan seeks to exploit disunity, while divine promise ensures victory for the steadfast.
